document: NIST AI 100-1: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
retrieval_status: Official NIST PDF and NIST AIRC HTML Core both retrieved successfully through the web connector. Exact statements were cross-checked between the two.
version_note: The AIRC page says AI RMF 1.0 is being updated and a revised version is in progress. This review uses the published AI RMF 1.0 (2023) Core, not a draft revision or the GenAI Profile.
quote_normalization: Line-wrapping, PDF discretionary hyphenation and capitalization of function names normalized; substantive wording preserved. Official texts are U.S. federal government works.

GV.1.2.text: The characteristics of trustworthy AI are integrated into organizational policies, processes, procedures, and practices.

GV.2.1.text: Roles and responsibilities and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are documented and are clear to individuals and teams throughout the organization.

GV.3.2.text: Policies and procedures are in place to define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight of AI systems.
GV.3.2.purpose: Comparison candidate only; not an automatically supported replacement for GV.2.1.

MP.3.5.text: Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies from the GOVERN function.
MP.3.5.purpose: Comparison candidate only; detecting an oversight bypass alone does not establish an oversight process.

MP.5.2.text: Practices and personnel for supporting regular engagement with relevant AI actors and integrating feedback about positive, negative, and unanticipated impacts are in place and documented.

MG.1.3.text: Responses to the AI risks deemed high priority, as identified by the MAP function, are developed, planned, and documented. Risk response options can include mitigating, transferring, avoiding, or accepting.

MG.2.2.text: Mechanisms are in place and applied to sustain the value of deployed AI systems.

MG.2.3.text: Procedures are followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified.

MG.2.4.text: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.
